title: The Favourite chair by the fire
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：favourite　|　正文 349 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 favourite 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the headmaster wrote of ① a favourite chair by the fire in the record, and everybody in the school said at once that it was ② so favourite that nobody in the school would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the headmaster, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the favourite ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the favourite chair by the fire that anybody there had ever seen, or so the record for October 1947 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too favourite to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the student who had come to help; the favourite ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bell at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a favourite song of the old man, and said that no student in his right mind would call it ⑥ as favourite as the song of the old man they had once had in the old school. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was favourite or not, and he said so.

By 1960 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something favourite, and nothing besides. The student from the next school called the whole plan ⑧ quite favourite; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the favourite ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1963, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another favourite chair by the fire in the same record, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less favourite than anybody had expected. ⑩ The favourite song of the old man that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1965, was the one she could never quite name; the favourite ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 最喜爱（前置定语 a favourite chair by the fire：1953 年校长在学籍册里记下的那件最喜爱的椅子）
B. adj. 最喜爱／最受喜爱（两处加强说法：so favourite that … 与 no less favourite than …）
C. adj. 最喜爱／最受喜爱（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 最喜爱（表语 too favourite to do：母亲觉得它太最喜爱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 最受喜爱（前置定语 a favourite song of the old man：叔叔把整件事称作一桩最受喜爱的那支歌）
F. adj. 最受喜爱（同级比较 as favourite as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩老人最爱的那支歌相比）
G. adj. 最受喜爱（后置定语 something favourite：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 最受喜爱（受程度副词修饰 quite favourite：那位学生的评价）

items.q: a favourite chair by the fire
the favourite chair by the fire that
a favourite song of the old man
The favourite song of the old man that

answers.why: favourite 意为“最喜爱”，1953 年校长在学籍册里记下的是“一件最喜爱的椅子”，此处作前置定语 a favourite chair by the fire。
favourite 意为“最喜爱”，此处用 so favourite that 结构，说它最喜爱到学堂里没人敢靠近。
favourite 意为“最喜爱”，学籍册上 十月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的最喜爱火炉边最中意的椅子，等于最高级的说法。
favourite 意为“最喜爱”，母亲认为这件东西“太最喜爱了，谁也用不上”，too favourite to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
favourite 意为“最受喜爱”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩最受喜爱的那支歌”，此处作前置定语 a favourite song of the old man。
favourite 意为“最受喜爱”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩老人最爱的那支歌一样最受喜爱”，同级比较用 as favourite as。
favourite 意为“最受喜爱”，学籍册上那半行字要的是“最受喜爱的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something favourite。
favourite 意为“最受喜爱”，邻学堂来的那位学生认为这套计划“相当最受喜爱”，quite 修饰原级 favourite。
favourite 意为“最受喜爱”，no less favourite than 表示“其最受喜爱不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之最受喜爱不亚于任何人的预料。
favourite 意为“最受喜爱”，母亲 1965 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的最受喜爱那支歌”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1953 年，校长在学籍册里记下了一件最喜爱的椅子。（a favourite chair by the fire）
它最喜爱到学堂里没有一个人敢靠近。（so favourite that …）
母亲觉得它太最喜爱，谁也用不上。（too favourite to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩最受喜爱的那支歌。（a favourite song of the old man）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩老人最爱的那支歌一样最受喜爱。（as favourite as …）
到了 1960 年，学籍册上只剩半行字：要的是一件最受喜爱的东西。（something favourite）
answers: In 1953 the headmaster wrote of a favourite chair by the fire in the record.
It was so favourite that nobody in the school would go near it.
My mother thought it too favourite to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a favourite song of the old man.
He said nobody would call it as favourite as the song of the old man they had once had.
By 1960 the record asked for nothing but something favourite.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 favourite 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1953 the headmaster wrote of a favourite chair by the fire in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the favourite chair by the fire that anybody there had ever seen, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too favourite to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a favourite song of the old man, and nobody argued with him.
The student from the next school called the plan quite favourite, and everybody laughed.
The favourite ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
